name: Paper Crumble
description: Interactive WebGL image that crumples like a sheet of paper while you press and hold it, with draggable motion, soft shadow and keyboard support. Releasing restores, keeps creases, or leaves it crumpled.
contents: Three.js canvas rendering the image as a deformable paper mesh with a front and optional back face
Invisible button covering the scene that receives pointer and keyboard input
Fallback img shown while loading or when WebGL fails, plus a screen reader status text
behavior: Press and hold to crumple the paper with a spring animation, release to restore, keep creases, or stay crumpled
Dragging while held moves and tilts the paper within a radius, and it can return to origin on release
Keyboard: hold Space or Enter to crumple, arrow keys to move, Escape to reset
Rendering pauses when offscreen or the tab is hidden, and recovers from WebGL context loss
Falls back to a plain image if the texture or WebGL fails, and reports through onError
editableByProps: Image, back image, alt text, paper size, scene height and image fit
Crumple strength, speeds, fold count, sharpness, wrinkle depth and crease strength
Paper color, roughness, grain, light intensity and angle, shadow
Drag behavior, rotation, release behavior, random seed, mesh detail, disabled and reset

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the aria label and keyboard shortcuts
needsCodeEdit.where: keyDown handler and the aria-label of the button in the returned JSX

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the loading fallback image layout
needsCodeEdit.where: img element rendered when status is not ready, using --pc-image-width and --pc-image-height CSS variables

fixed: Requires the three package and a browser with WebGL, client only ('use client')
Component is exported as PaperCrumple and needs a src image, otherwise nothing is shown
Images are loaded as textures, so cross-origin images need CORS headers
Uses Tailwind utility classes for layout
Scene fills the parent width with fixed pixel sceneHeight, so on small screens width and height should be reduced
Pointer based hold interaction, uses touch-none on the hit area which blocks scroll gestures over the paper

options.look: Paper smooths back to flat after release
Paper flattens but keeps visible crease marks
options.useWhen: You want a lasting trace of the interaction
A destructive, one-way effect, reset through resetKey
